recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If this behavior regresses in a modern publisher, handle it in the current IG Publisher/FHIR Java tooling project; no FHIR core source edit is indicated for this issue.
issue_request: FHIR-15830 asked that the IG Publisher accept a logical model's canonical URI in ElementDefinition.type.code when a logical model embeds another logical model, instead of treating that URI as an unresolved reference and forcing use of Reference/targetProfile.
initial_application: Jira comments record reporter confirmation that the error was fixed in the same-day build and cite svn revision 13543. The corresponding git-svn commit, 25b1e21b49d7b43a8ae1abcac29f9e14ddc39f5b, changed old in-repository Java validation, element model, FHIRPath, ShEx, and IG Publisher helper code to resolve absolute StructureDefinition URLs rather than always prefixing the core StructureDefinition namespace.
additional_context: FHIR-12245 had already established the underlying specification rule by changing ElementDefinition.type.code to URI and allowing absolute URLs in logical models. Current source still says absolute URLs are only allowed in logical models, limits custom type codes to logical models through sdf-19, and describes the binding as including logical model types. The old Java IG Publisher and implementation paths touched by svn revision 13543 are no longer active files in this checkout, so any modern publisher regression belongs in current external tooling rather than FHIR spec source.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The reconciliation published an empty external-repo audit commit on the combined branch documenting that the current spec source is already correct and the applied implementation fix is outside the active FHIR source tree.

related_jiras.note: Established that ElementDefinition.type.code is a URI and that logical models may use absolute StructureDefinition URLs as type codes.
